subject: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom R. <tom.r@designpartners.io>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes

Team —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Two quick asks to land before Wednesday's exec preview:

1) QBR deck: I attached the v0.9 deck and an action tracker. Please review slides in your area and add any critical metrics by EOD Tuesday. Key gaps I saw: Dedicated latency SLA graph needs a one-slide narrative, and the cost-per-token chart needs normalization across models.

2) Exception owners: there are three active exceptions (KV cache regressions, Dedicated autoscale flakiness, and EU region rollout delay). I listed proposed owners in the tracker — confirm or propose alternates.

3) Exec asks: we need 1–2 concise asks (decision or resource) for leadership. If you have items, put a 1-line ask + impact in the tracker.

Attachments: QBR-Deck-v0.9.pdf (stub), QBR-action-tracker.xlsx (stub)

Note: Sarah, Tom — thanks for joining the sync. If you have any customer-facing concerns to call out in the QBR (risk windows, migration timelines), drop them directly in the deck comments.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Sr. Product Manager, Red wood Inference
ava.chen@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes

Ava —

Thanks for the clear asks. A few notes inline:

- QBR deck: I'll take the Dedicated latency slide and add a short failure-mode callout. Expect a slide update by Tue 3pm PT.

- Exception owners: I can take the KV cache regression (owner: k_iyer). Marissa, can you own the EU rollout delay with the infra PM?

- Exec ask proposal: Request 6 weeks of burst infra credits for Dedicated capacity to support our spike tests (business impact: reduces SLA misses for high-throughput customers and avoids immediate partner escalations). I'll add a 1-line ask to the tracker.

Couple of quick questions: is the cost normalization supposed to be per-100k tokens or per-invocation? I can normalize both but need to know which exec narrative we prefer.

Onward,
Karthik
Director, Serving Product

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes

Ava / Karthik —

I've updated the tracker with owners and ETA for each active exception. Summary: 

- KV cache regressions: owner = karthik_iyer, mitigation plan + test matrix by 11/6.
- Dedicated autoscale flakiness: owner = marissa_cole + infra PM (Nina Patel), tentative rollback window scheduled 11/5 02:00–04:00 PT.
- EU rollout delay: owner = marissa_cole (coord w/ infra + legal), timeline revised to 11/18 pending KMS approval.

Also added a short blurb for the Dedicated latency slide: current median is 38ms (p95 120ms) for text-generation-1 x86 quantized. I tried to keep the language non-technical for execs — please review and shorten as needed.

Sarah — I left a flagged item about the cutover window that affects your migration. If that is a blocker, call it out and we'll prioritize.

Attaching the tracker snapshot as a stub in the deck.

—Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes

Thanks Marissa — that ETA cadence looks good.

Karthik: please normalize to per-100k tokens for the deck (execs prefer a per-workload roll-up). Add a 1-line footnote for per-invocation numbers in the appendix.

Sarah: can you confirm whether the 11/5 rollback window is acceptable for Acme's migration? If it's a blocker we'll move the window earlier and add more validation tests.

I'll consolidate final deck edits by Tue 4pm PT and send the exec preview at 5pm. If you need me to make any wording changes for the ask language, ping me directly.

Thanks,
Ava

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly XFN follow-ups — QBR pulse, exception owners and canary notes

All —

Thanks for the updates and for taking owners. A couple of operational asks before the exec preview: 

- Please add a 1-line risk statement for each exception in the tracker (impact + probability). Execs want clarity on "what happens if we don't act".
- Karthik, include a short rollback criteria bullet so leadership can sign off on the proposed 11/5 window.
- Marissa, confirm the infra PM and put the rollback runbook link in the tracker.

I'll review the final deck at 4:30pm PT and prep the two exec-level asks to present (burst credits + temporary SLA exception for EU ramp).

If no blockers, I think we can land this for Wednesday.

—Vivek
VP, Product Operations
